title: Is your nervous system shutting down from stress?
intro: When stress becomes overwhelming, some nervous systems stop fighting and start shutting down. This can look like avoidance, exhaustion, procrastination, numbness, or feeling mentally stuck. This check-in is designed to help you understand how stress-related shutdown or freeze responses may currently be affecting you.

options.text: Frozen when trying to start things
Tempted to avoid stressful situations completely
Mentally stuck and unable to move forward
Overwhelmed internally while still trying to function

questions.text: When life feels stressful, I usually:

options.text: Overthink so much that I feel stuck
Quietly push through while struggling internally
I don't know how to begin
Avoiding things feels easier than facing them
My brain feels trapped in stress
Everything feels heavy but I keep functioning anyway

questions.text: People around me probably see me as:
What do you need most right now?

options.text: Gentle structure and small starting points
Support without needing to explain everything

a.description: You struggle beginning tasks and feel mentally frozen when overwhelmed. The first step often feels like the hardest part — and that's okay.

b.description: You disconnect from stress or difficult emotions through avoidance. Stepping away can feel like the only way to cope when things feel like too much.

c.description: You feel trapped mentally and struggle moving forward or making decisions. Your mind is working overtime trying to find a way through.

d.description: Long-term stress has turned into mental and emotional exhaustion. Your system has been running on empty and is asking for real recovery.

e.description: You are still functioning quietly while feeling deeply overwhelmed internally. You carry more than most people realize, and you deserve support too.
